ops.title: roll darwin: prevent wake-pipe inheritance across exec
ops.description:
Owner: desk-roll-on-install implementation caller.
Review scope: staged diff; source inspection only; no tests run.
Severity: minor
Evidence: plugins/long-running/lr/internal/roll/watch_darwin.go:25 — unix.Pipe leaves both descriptors inheritable. Desk subprocesses can retain the writer, so closing the parent writer at line 29 does not generate EV_EOF while such a descendant remains alive; the watch goroutine and its fds remain blocked. Go os/pipe_unix.go:17-25 demonstrates ForkLock and CloseOnExec.
Next executable step: Create the wake pipe through os.Pipe or set CLOEXEC on both ends while holding syscall.ForkLock.

ops.text: Exec children do not inherit either wake-pipe end.
Canceling a watch releases its descriptors even while a launched child remains alive.
